documents.summary: Faculty guidelines from the Office for Academic Affairs explain what generative AI is, its limits (errors, bias), and advise instructors to experiment, talk with students, redesign assignments and use a syllabus statement. It ends with three suggested syllabus statements that run from open use with citation to a full ban.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines set no rule themselves; they advise faculty ("we recommend a syllabus statement on using AI") and offer three "Suggested Syllabus Statements on AI Use" from allowed with referencing to "AI use is not allowed", so the choice sits with instructors: delegates with tiers.

documents.summary: Graduate School guidance for committee-based exams, projects, theses and dissertations. It asks each program to set its own limits, strongly discourages over-reliance, requires disclosure and student responsibility, and gives four example program statements from partial permission to a full ban, plus privacy and copyright cautions.
documents.stance_why: The document tells programs to "develop specific parameters regarding the degree to which the use of generative AI is allowable" and supplies example statements from permissive to "not permitted at any phase", so it sets no single stance and passes the decision to programs and committees: delegates with example tiers. The only university-wide rules are disclosure and student responsibility.

notes: Reconciled consensus of coder A and coder B. Coder A. Full Generative AI Policy (May 2026) not located; AI Hub FAQ stands in. No computing-unit or course documents screened in. Provost page text includes many unrelated policies; only the generative AI guidelines section was coded. Coder B. Only the three included university-layer documents were coded; no school or computing-unit policy was found, and the full May 2026 Generative AI Policy text was not available (the FAQ stands in for it). Graduate School text contains ligature characters (e.g. 'specific'), so some anchors were chosen to avoid them. Repeated syllabus-template paragraphs in the provost guidelines (template 2 verify/disclosure text, UA AI Experience link) were coded once as exact repeats. Template 3 sentence 'Use of any generative AI tool in this course constitutes academic misconduct' was coded P01 rather than P36 because it defines the ban.
